title: Copilot Studio: block maker-provided credentials for tool authentication
summary: Hold: the briefing incorrectly says that no automation is documented for blocking maker credentials. Microsoft documents a writable Dataverse organization setting for that restriction, with a Web API update operation and a CLI route; the other checked claims are supported.

claims.claim: The credential control is reached through Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments (or Environment groups) > environment > Settings > Product > Features > Copilot Studio agents > Control maker credential options.

claims.claim: The environment sharing control is reached through Power Platform admin center > Manage > Environments > environment > Settings > Features > Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials.
claims.quote: Go to Manage > Environments, and then select the environment that you want to configure. ... Select Settings, and then select Features. ... Find Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials.

claims.claim: The Threat detection route selects the Environment groups or Environments tab and target before Set up and the Don't let makers share agents with their own credentials embedded (recommended) option.
claims.quote: select Security, and then select Threat detection. ... Select Sharing agent with embedded maker credentials. ... In the Environment groups tab, select the environment group ... Select Set up. ... Don't let makers share agents with their own credentials embedded (recommended)

claims.claim: The maker-side path is Copilot Studio > Agents > agent > Tools > tool > Details > Authentication.
claims.quote: select Agents, and then select your agent. ... go to your agent's Tools page and select the tool. ... Details ... Authentication | Runs the tool with the user's credentials (End user, the default) or the maker's credentials (Maker-provided).

claims.where: controls[0].api; Governance controls; Open questions; Governance guidance: After rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft Learn documents no PowerShell, REST or CLI operation for preventing maker-provided tool credentials.
claims.quote: Update ... PATCH /organizations(organizationid) ... Writable columns/attributes ... BlockCopilotAuthorAuthentication ... Prevent makers from allowing end-users to use their credentials during authentication to use connectors, actions, flows, and triggers that are connected to an agent
claims.fix: Set controls[0].api to kind 'rest', call 'PATCH /organizations(<organizationid>)', docs 'https://learn.microsoft.com/power-apps/developer/data-platform/reference/entities/organization'. Add to its note: 'For a Dataverse environment, the request body sets blockcopilotauthorauthentication to true to prevent maker credential reuse.' Replace the no-automation prose with that sentence and remove the question and checklist instruction premised on no documented operation. The reference lists this Boolean as writable, describes the restriction, and documents Update; https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/developer/cli/reference/env#pac-env-update-settings also documents updating organization settings by name.

claims.quote: Searched: "Sharing agents with embedded maker credentials" PowerShell API environment settings Dataverse; opened configure-sharing-agents-embedded-maker-credentials, Organization reference and Environment Management Settings update reference. No deciding property found.

claims.claim: No automation is documented for the Threat detection embedded-credential sharing control.

claims.claim: No automation is documented for a given tool's maker-versus-end-user Authentication choice.
claims.quote: Searched: Copilot Studio tool Authentication Maker-provided End user Dataverse botcomponent Web API configure authentication; opened add-tools-custom-agent and botcomponent reference; searched the reference for authentication, credentials and connections. No deciding property found.

claims.claim: Control maker credential options lets administrators allow end-user credentials, maker credentials, or both.
claims.quote: You choose whether makers can select to use their own credentials for authenticating tool connections, to use the end-user's credentials, or to have access to both.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Data exposure; rationale: risk
claims.claim: A connector or flow tool configured with maker credentials authenticates with the maker's credentials when another user uses the agent.
claims.quote: When someone uses the agent, the agent uses the maker's credentials, not the end user's credentials, to authenticate with connected services.

claims.where: Why it matters; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: Maker credential reuse can let users retrieve information or perform actions permitted only to the maker.
claims.quote: an end user might retrieve information or perform actions that only the maker's account is permitted to do.

claims.claim: Enforcing end-user credentials makes actions run with the user's permissions rather than the maker's.
claims.quote: The action runs under the end-user's identity. If the user lacks permission for something, the agent is unable to do it on their behalf - by design.

claims.where: summary; What's changing; Why it matters; controls[0].note
claims.claim: Learn warns that enforcement immediately turns off makers' ability to select their credentials.
claims.quote: the feature immediately turns off the maker's ability to select their credentials for authenticating tools within the environment or environment group.

claims.claim: Enforcing the restriction changes all tools for all agents in affected environments to require end-user credentials at runtime.
claims.quote: All tools for all agents in the impacted environments instantly change to require end-user credentials at runtime.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance guidance; rationale: impact
claims.claim: Affected users are prompted to sign in to connected services when needed, including in new conversations.
claims.quote: Enforcing the use of end-user credentials prompts the end user to sign in (to the relevant service or connector) when needed. ... If the user is already signed in ... the agent might use that existing authentication session.

claims.claim: No stored maker credentials are used at runtime when end-user credentials are enforced.
claims.quote: No stored maker credentials are used at run time, aligning the agent's behavior with the end user's actual permissions.

claims.where: Risk assessment: Security & identity; Scope; Governance guidance: At rollout
claims.claim: Environment group credential policy overrides individual environment settings.
claims.quote: you can't individually disable it for one environment in that group - environment group settings override any environment settings.

claims.claim: Individual environment credential options are unavailable when configuration must be performed on the group.
claims.quote: If the environment is in a group, the options are unavailable and a message directs you to configure the setting for the group, not the individual environment.

claims.claim: Blocking maker credentials requires real-time user interaction and a live user sign-in for tool calls.
claims.quote: agents require real-time user interaction because each tool call must be authenticated with a live user sign-in.

claims.claim: Scheduled-event agents fail due to missing credentials after maker credentials are blocked.
claims.quote: agents triggered by scheduled or autonomous events, or that attempt to run in the background, fail due to missing credentials.

claims.claim: The separate embedded-credential sharing control governs sharing and publishing, not runtime.
